candidates.label: Embed immutable source selectors in each authored form
evidence: The refined authored-form envelope already requires provenance as NonEmpty<ImmutableSourceSelector>.
Embedded selectors keep each form self-contained and allow offline validation without resolving another ontology or registry object.
The thin-kernel and precedent reviews reject ornamental concepts that do not alter compilation or validation.

candidates.label: Reference one immutable canonical provenance record
evidence: A separately versioned immutable record can deduplicate a source-selector set shared by many authored forms.
The record can bind exact source identities, selectors, byte domains, sizes, digests, and producer receipt once.
This option requires a new record identity, resolver, lifecycle, schema, and validation owner before forms remain self-contained by reference.

candidates.label: Store both inline selectors and a provenance reference as co-authoritative
rejectionReasons: Two co-authoritative provenance representations introduce disagreement and precedence ambiguity.
No current owner rule defines which bytes win when the inline selectors and referenced record diverge.

candidates.label: Store only a provenance digest
rejectionReasons: A digest without source identity, selector, byte domain, size, and version is not reproducibly resolvable.
Digest equality alone does not establish source ownership, semantics, admission, or authority.

candidates.label: Defer canonical provenance representation
evidence: Deferral preserves the candidate but keeps exact authored-form schemas, fixture digests, and ontology source-binding obligations blocked.

candidates.label: Stop the composition-form Decision Gate
evidence: Stopping preserves current source and candidate bytes and authorizes no downstream mutation.
